latest_nl_proof:
Fix h >= 0, and let A be the set of numerical semigroups of genus h. For each integer r >= 0, let A_r = {Lambda in A : e(Lambda) = r}. By definition, n_h(r) = |A_r|.

First we justify finiteness of all displayed sums.

If h = 0, then the complement of Lambda in the nonnegative integers has size 0, so Lambda is the whole set of nonnegative integers. Thus A has exactly one element. In this semigroup, 1 is the only minimal generator, because every x > 1 can be written as 1 + (x-1) with both summands positive and in Lambda. Since F(Lambda) = -1 in this case, the only effective generator is 1, so e(Lambda) = 1, and therefore s(Lambda) <= 1. Hence all displayed sums are finite when h = 0.

Now assume h >= 1. Take any Lambda in A, and write F = F(Lambda). Since genus(Lambda) = h, the set of gaps of Lambda has exactly h elements. Because h >= 1, this gap set is nonempty and finite, so F exists.

Among the integers 1,2,...,F, exactly h are gaps; one of them is F itself. Therefore among 1,2,...,F-1 there are exactly h-1 gaps, and hence exactly F-h non-gaps. If a is a non-gap in {1,...,F-1}, then F-a is a gap: otherwise a and F-a would both be positive elements of Lambda, so their sum F would belong to Lambda, contradicting the definition of F. The map a -> F-a is injective, so the number F-h of non-gaps in {1,...,F-1} is at most the number h-1 of gaps there. Thus F-h <= h-1, i.e. F <= 2h-1.

So every gap of every genus-h numerical semigroup lies in the finite set {1,2,...,2h-1}. Since a numerical semigroup is completely determined by its gap set, there are only finitely many genus-h numerical semigroups. Therefore A is finite.

Now fix Lambda in A, and let m = m(Lambda). If x in Lambda satisfies x > F(Lambda) + m, then x-m > F(Lambda), so x-m belongs to Lambda; also x-m > 0 because F(Lambda) >= 1. Hence x = m + (x-m) expresses x as a sum of two positive elements of Lambda, so x is not a minimal generator. Therefore every effective generator x of Lambda satisfies F(Lambda) < x <= F(Lambda) + m. There are only finitely many such integers, so e(Lambda) is finite. Since s(Lambda) counts only some effective generators, s(Lambda) <= e(Lambda), so s(Lambda) is finite as well.

Because A is finite, only finitely many values r = e(Lambda) occur, so only finitely many n_h(r) are nonzero. Hence every displayed sum in the statement is finite.

Now we prove the identities. Since the sum over A is finite, we may split it termwise:

sum over Lambda in A of ( e(Lambda)(e(Lambda)-1)/2 + s(Lambda) )
= sum over Lambda in A of e(Lambda)(e(Lambda)-1)/2 + sum over Lambda in A of s(Lambda).

By the definition of S(h), the second sum is exactly S(h).

For the first sum, the sets A_r form a disjoint partition of A, and e(Lambda) = r for every Lambda in A_r. Therefore

sum over Lambda in A of e(Lambda)(e(Lambda)-1)/2
= sum over r >= 0 of sum over Lambda in A_r of r(r-1)/2
= sum over r >= 0 of |A_r| * r(r-1)/2
= sum over r >= 0 of n_h(r) * r(r-1)/2.

Combining these equalities gives

sum over all genus-h Lambda of ( e(Lambda)(e(Lambda)-1)/2 + s(Lambda) )
= sum over r >= 0 of n_h(r) * r(r-1)/2 + S(h).

Finally, since the A_r are a disjoint partition of A,

N(h) = |A| = sum over r >= 0 of |A_r| = sum over r >= 0 of n_h(r).

This proves both stated identities, and also proves that all displayed sums are finite.
role_in_parent: Regroups the global parent sum by the effective-generator distribution and identifies the unweighted grouped count with N(h).
statement_nl: Let h be a nonnegative integer. A numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers containing 0, and its genus is the number of nonnegative integers not belonging to it. For a numerical semigroup Lambda, let F(Lambda) be the largest integer not in Lambda, with the convention F(Lambda) = -1 for the whole set of nonnegative integers. Let m(Lambda) be the least positive element of Lambda. A minimal generator of Lambda is a positive element x of Lambda that cannot be written as a+b with positive a,b in Lambda. An effective generator of Lambda is a minimal generator x with x > F(Lambda), and let e(Lambda) be the number of effective generators of Lambda. For an effective generator x of Lambda, let c_x(Lambda) be the set obtained from Lambda by removing x. Let s(Lambda) be the number of effective generators x such that m(Lambda) + x is a minimal generator of c_x(Lambda). Let N(h) be the number of numerical semigroups of genus h. For each integer r >= 0, let n_h(r) be the number of genus-h numerical semigroups Lambda with e(Lambda) = r. Let S(h) be the sum of s(Lambda) over all genus-h numerical semigroups Lambda. Then the sum, over all genus-h numerical semigroups Lambda, of e(Lambda)(e(Lambda)-1)/2 + s(Lambda) is equal to the sum, over all integers r >= 0, of n_h(r) * r(r-1)/2 plus S(h). Also N(h) is equal to the sum, over all integers r >= 0, of n_h(r). All displayed sums are finite.

domain_restrictions: Λ is a numerical semigroup: cofinite additive submonoid of Z_{>=0} with 0 ∈ Λ
F(Λ) is the largest integer not in Λ, with convention F(Λ)=-1 if Λ=Z_{>=0}
m(Λ) is the least positive element of Λ (so implicitly Λ has at least one positive element)
minimal generator definition requires: x ∈ Λ, x>0, and x cannot be written as a+b with a,b>0 and a,b ∈ Λ
effective generator: x is a minimal generator and x > F(Λ)
c_x(Λ) is defined as the set obtained from Λ by removing x (so x must be an element of Λ)
s(Λ) counts effective generators x such that m(Λ)+x is a minimal generator of c_x(Λ)
r is restricted to integers r>=0 in the definition of n_h(r) and in the r-indexed sum
all sums stated are finite (so in particular n_h(r)=0 for all sufficiently large r, and only finitely many Λ contribute nontrivially)
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim:
For each fixed h ∈ Z_{>=0}, summing over all numerical semigroups Λ with genus(Λ)=h, the quantity e(Λ)(e(Λ)-1)/2 + s(Λ) satisfies
∑_{Λ: genus(Λ)=h} ( e(Λ)(e(Λ)-1)/2 + s(Λ) ) = ∑_{r∈Z_{>=0}} n_h(r)·( r(r-1)/2 ) + S(h),
where n_h(r) counts genus-h semigroups with e(Λ)=r and S(h)=∑_{Λ: genus(Λ)=h} s(Λ). Also, N(h)=|{Λ: genus(Λ)=h}| satisfies
N(h) = ∑_{r∈Z_{>=0}} n_h(r).
All displayed sums are finite.
quantifier_order: ∀h ∈ Z_{>=0} (h fixed as the parameter for all subsequent definitions and identities)
∑ over Λ such that genus(Λ)=h (Λ ranges over numerical semigroups of genus h)
∑ over r ∈ Z_{>=0} (r indexes the partition by e(Λ)=r)
For each effective generator x of Λ (x witnesses the condition counted by s(Λ))

variables.name: h
variables.role: fixed genus parameter; all semigroups considered have genus h

variables.domain: cofinite additive submonoid of Z_{>=0} containing 0
variables.name: Lambda
variables.role: ranged over all numerical semigroups with genus(Lambda)=h

variables.name: r
variables.role: effective-generator count value; indexes the partition by e(Lambda)=r

variables.name: x
variables.role: element serving as a candidate effective generator; used to define c_x(Lambda) and s(Lambda)
variables.type: positive integer element of a numerical semigroup

witness_dependencies: effective-generator membership of x depends on Λ through both: (i) minimality of x in Λ and (ii) the inequality x > F(Λ)
e(Λ) is determined by counting effective generators x of Λ; hence e(Λ) depends on F(Λ) and the minimal generators of Λ
c_x(Λ) depends on both x and Λ
the condition counted by s(Λ) for a given effective generator x depends on m(Λ) and on minimal-generator status of m(Λ)+x inside c_x(Λ)
n_h(r) depends on h (via restricting to genus(Λ)=h) and on r (via the condition e(Λ)=r)
S(h)=∑_{Λ: genus(Λ)=h} s(Λ) depends on h
